body.x: The Seoul Business Agency (SBA, President and CEO Hyunwoo Kim) held the “CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion Launch Ceremony” on the 1st. It reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring a successful participation at CES 2026.

CES (Consumer Electronics Show) is the world’s largest technology exhibition, held every early January in Las Vegas, the United States, where global corporations such as Google and Samsung, along with startups, present future technology visions and cutting-edge products and services.

CES 2026 will take place from January 6 to 9 next year. The Seoul Pavilion will be located in Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition zone, and will operate as a dedicated pavilion showcasing advanced startups based in Seoul.

The Seoul Metropolitan Government and the Seoul Business Agency plan to promote Seoul startups’ global innovation by leveraging the collective strength of Seoul’s startup ecosystem, and to support international expansion through programs such as business matching and a global startup IR pitching competition.

The CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion will host 70 startups, with participation from 19 Seoul-based startup support organizations, including the lead organization SBA, district governments, related institutions, and universities. In addition, 70 university student supporters will be selected and matched one-to-one with participating companies to provide on-site support.

The 19 participating organizations include four district offices—Gangnam-gu Office, Gwanak-gu Office, Guro-gu Office, and Geumcheon-gu Office—six Seoul Metropolitan Government–affiliated startup support institutions, including the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), Seoul Campus Town Enterprise Growth Center, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Social Venture Hub, Seoul AI Hub, and Seoul Fintech Lab (Yeouido), as well as nine universities based in Seoul: Konkuk University, Kyung Hee University, Kwangwoon University, Sogang University, Seoul National University, Sungkyunkwan University, Yonsei University, Ewha Womans University, and Chung-Ang University.
The 70 companies exhibiting in the Seoul Pavilion consist of startups with advanced technology–based products and services in fields such as AI, mobility, and healthcare.

body.cap: Overview of the CES 2025 Seoul Pavilion held earlier this year. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: To enhance external recognition and global visibility of Seoul startups’ innovation, SBA provided support for Innovation Award applications, including advanced consulting, for approximately two months from July to August. As a result, a total of 17 companies, including one Best of Innovation award winner, were selected for the CES 2026 Innovation Awards. The CES Innovation Awards are presented annually by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), the exhibition organizer, to technologies and products recognized for technological excellence, design, and innovation.

The Best of Innovation award was won by Studio Lab Co., Ltd., a member of the SBA-operated Innovation Award community, which proudly stood alongside global conglomerates such as Samsung and Qualcomm. The achievement is especially meaningful, as the award is granted to only about 30 companies worldwide each year.
SBA operates a CES Innovation Award community for award-winning companies and plans to continue follow-up support programs, including inter-company collaboration.

In addition, SBA plans to offer a broader range of business programs for participating companies, including pre-event and on-site investment and buyer matching, cross-country IR pitching and networking, investor networking events, exhibition booths, and on-site IR pitching, and on-site support by university student supporters.

SBA will closely manage the process from online matching before the exhibition to successful on-site meetings with buyers expected to attend CES. Participating companies will also receive sales opportunities, including participation in IR pitching sessions on the Seoul Pavilion stage.

The “University Student Supporters” program, which matches outstanding students selected by partner universities with participating companies on a one-to-one basis, will also be operated. This year, 70 global talents fluent in both English and Korean will be deployed on site, selected from nine Seoul-based universities and graduates of universities in Las Vegas, the United States.

body.cap: Visitors at the CES 2025 Seoul Pavilion held earlier this year. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Participating companies will also gain comprehensive promotional and investment opportunities through the Global Innovation Forum, a national pavilion networking program hosted by the SBA. One outstanding company will be selected to compete in the forum’s flagship session, the Global Startup IR Pitching Competition.

Support will also be provided for participation in a Korean entrepreneur conference held near the CES venue in San Francisco, as well as the 2026 UKF 82 Startup Summit scheduled for January 9 to 12. Participating companies will receive admission tickets, and one outstanding company will have the opportunity to participate in an on-site pitching session. UKF is a nonprofit organization that supports the growth and mutual support of Korean entrepreneurs and startup ecosystem members, co-chaired by Gihah Lee, CEO of unicorn startup Sazze Partners, and Seju Jung, CEO of Noom.

In addition, SBA will provide a range of pre-education programs to maximize CES participation outcomes, from basic CES orientation to sales know-how, reflecting business trends such as LinkedIn. Various promotional programs will also be operated for supported companies. Each year, SBA develops new programs to enhance promotional impact, and this year it will introduce the ‘Innovation Award Showcase’ and ‘Media Center’ within the Seoul Pavilion.

The newly introduced Seoul Pavilion Innovation Award Showcase will serve as a promotional space for Innovation Award–winning companies. It will be placed at the pavilion’s main entrance to capture visitors’ attention. The Media Center, a filming and interview space inside the pavilion, will function as a hub for producing new media content that highlights exhibiting companies.

Selected outstanding companies will also have the opportunity to participate in CES’s official media event, Unveiled, which is aimed at major global media outlets, to maximize media exposure. SBA will further enhance media visibility for exhibiting companies by distributing press releases through collaboration with CES’s official global media partners and specialized outlets.

body.cap: SBA President and CEO Hyunwoo Kim delivers opening remarks at the CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion launch ceremony. | Provided by Seoul Business Agency

body.x: Meanwhile, the CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion Launch Ceremony, held on December 1 at SBA Hall, served as a declaration of the launch of a “one team” comprising companies, institutions, and university student supporters, and announced the pavilion’s operational plan. During the ceremony, participants received detailed guidance on key support items, exhibition preparation, and upcoming schedules, as well as training sessions to share CES participation know-how and strengthen global business capabilities.

The ceremony was attended by key officials from the 19 partner organizations, including SBA President and CEO Hyunwoo Kim and Center Director Mija Oh of Konkuk University’s WE人 Education Center. University student supporters for the Seoul Pavilion also attended, familiarizing themselves with exhibition participation details alongside their matched companies and strengthening their shared commitment.

Hyunwoo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency, said, “CES is a stage where global big tech companies and the startup ecosystem converge, and it offers the optimal opportunity for Seoul startups to connect directly with global investors, partners, and media.” He added, “SBA will spare no effort to provide a platform that enables Seoul companies to leap into the global market, using the Seoul Pavilion as a stepping stone.”
